messages:
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] ALERT: High GPU OOM rate on inference-service (us-east-1). Severity: P1. Affected: hosted model pool 'g4-8x'.

maria_g: seeing spike in container restarts across replicas. SIGKILL from OOM, several restarts in last 2m. Logs show prefill loops on large prompts.

kevin_p: confirming, nvidia-smi shows memory at 40GB (device 0/48GB) then sudden drop. dmesg includes oom-killer messages. Also seeing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in some traces.

sanjay_r: can we identify top offending requests? 

maria_g: tailing request logs -> pattern: very long system/user messages (context windows 250k tokens) coming from a single tenant (org-458). Prefill allocs spike due to full KV cache.

devon_t: tagging @cs_amy for customer impact

cs_amy: pinged customer. They report slow requests and a few failures (~1% of calls) starting ~08:12 UTC. No PII; they confirm it's large batch uploads and long transcripts.

sanjay_r: immediate mitigation proposals:
- throttle prefill length client-side
- enable prefill streaming / trim prefixes
- route org-458 to a lower-memory model variant
- temporarily scale up dedicated pool or exclude noisy nodes

maria_g: let's do quick mitigations: 1) add route override for org-458 -> small-quant-7b 2) set per-tenant prefill limit 3) cordon node-9 (highest error rate) to stop restarts

kevin_p: working on node cordon and draining. kubectl:

``
kubectl cordon node-9
kubectl drain node-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
``

maria_g: applied routing override: org-458 -> small-quant-7b (dark-launch) and set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=512 for that tenant. Monitoring.

ops-bot: Automatic rollback policy: if error rate drops below threshold in 5m we keep changes; otherwise autoscale up.

sanjay_r: also enabling early-kv-eviction hotpatch on serving runtime (reduce per-request KV reserved pages):

``
PATCH runtime-config set kv_eviction_threshold=0.6
PATCH runtime-config set prefill_streaming=true
``

devon_t: oncall handoff: sanjay_r taking lead for mitigation, kevin_p for infra, maria_g for routing/serving. @oncall-bot please record escalation.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Pager duty incident pd-7821 assigned to sanjay_r.

maria_g: observing reduced memory spikes on cordoned nodes and fewer restarts. error rate dropped from 18% -> 4% in 6m.

cs_amy: customer update sent: "We identified encoding-heavy requests causing GPU memory exhaustion. We've routed your traffic to a lower-memory path and applied temporary limits. No data loss; will follow up with a permanent fix." (customer replied with :thumbsup:)

kevin_p: node-9 confirm rebooted and kernel logs show OOM events. We're investigating if kernel driver bug caused `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` or if purely memory pressure.

sanjay_r: monitoring for next 30m. action items:
- infra: scan nodes for CUDA driver mismatch and GPU ECC errors (kevin_p)
- serving: implement tenant prefill guardrails + per-tenant rate limiter (maria_g)
- product: consider default prefill cap + docs for large-context workloads (devon_t)

maria_g: creating follow-up tickets: INF-3982 (tenant guardrails), INF-3983 (runtime kv eviction tuning), INF-3984 (operator runbook updates). 

ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 08:45 UTC. Keeping incident channel open for postmortem.

sanjay_r: note for postmortem - long contexts causing sustained KV cache growth, combined with single-tenant burst and no prefill limit. Suggest automated detection of long-prefill patterns and proactive routing.

devon_t: agreed. I'll coordinate customer communication and prioritization for permanent mitigations.

maria_g: final status: traffic routed, node cordoned, runtime patch applied, error rate stabilized. Will keep watch and reopen if anomalies.

oncall-bot: Incident closed by sanjay_r at 09:05 UTC (follow-ups logged). 

maria_g: thanks all. Kudos to the quick cross-team coordination :clap:

sanjay_r: adding postmortem owner tag to devon_t. We'll aim for RCA within 72h.
